transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-20
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (CTO - Larkspur), Raul Ortega (Platform Eng), Sofia Alvarez (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial):
Larkspur is evaluating Redwood for their chat + code-assist features. Primary concern: fast time-to-first-token for a PLG onramp and data controls for user PII. They currently run on AWS EKS and call OpenAI; want a plan to get from PoC to ~50 QPS production.

Topics covered:
- Quickstart credits and expected time to first token
- Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved GPUs vs Private VPC deployment
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Performance targets and sample benchmarks
- Next steps for a pilot and who owns what

[00:00] Jordan Ellis: hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time, im jordan from redwood, im the account lead, with priya who is our systems eng, and we figured we'd run through a quick discovery to understand your ttft expectations and security constraints
[00:25] Maya Chen: hey jordan, thanks, yeah quick intro - im maya, cto at larkspur labs, we build an ai code-assist and chat assistant embedded inside our IDE, gonna be heavy on low latency and short prompts, we currently proxy through open a-i, but want more control and cost predictability
[00:40] Raul Ortega: hi all, raul here, platform eng, im focused on infra and cost, we run on eks, want to know if we can keep keys on our kms and if the private deploy is "on prem" or vpc option
[00:55] Priya Kapoor: great, thanks, quick note - we usually recommend start with hosted quickstart credits to get to first request in hours, then decide reserved/dedicated for steady throughput. tonight we'll ask about latency targets, throughput, data residency etc
[01:12] Jordan Ellis: one question for you maya - whats your timeline for getting a pilot live? are you thinking days/weeks/months?
[01:20] Maya Chen: ideally weeks, like a two to three week spike to validate latencies and some cost numbers, then an 8-12 week pilot for production readiness if things look good
[01:34] Raul Ortega: and for scale, target would be right now 10-20 QPS during beta, and we expect 50 QPS at launch, with P95 latency target sub 200ms for short prompts (50-150 tokens), is that realistic?
[01:52] Priya Kapoor: okay thats helpful. for hosted we have models that hit sub 200ms at small sequence lengths on our low-latency profiles; cost and batching matter. for 50 qps you'd likely want reserved/dedicated capacity or at least a dedicated pool for burst, or a mixed routing policy. we can show you a perf run and kernel choices that affect latency
[02:15] Maya Chen: what about kv cache? for the code-assist we want kv caching to avoid reprocessing previous tokens, how does redwood handle that?
[02:25] Priya Kapoor: we use prefix / KV cache - we call it KV cache in the runtime, and for private deployments the cache is local to the pod, while hosted we do distributed cache with secure keys, sometimes transcribed in logs as K-V cash by the transcriber ha. latency impact is small if cache hits are high
[02:45] Jordan Ellis: thought i'd ask about success criteria - what would make this pilot successful? cost per request below X, latency under threshold, or ease of rollout?
[02:55] Sofia Alvarez: success for us is three things: predictable token cost (we want a way to forecast monthly spend), latency <200ms p95, and end-to-end data controls for customer PII so nothing leaves our VPC without keys
[03:12] Jordan Ellis: noted. on the data controls piece - we have a private option (VPC + on-premlike bundles) that gives you a customer-managed control plane and KMS integration so keys never leave your tenancy. we also provide audit logs and per-token traceability in the console
[03:30] Raul Ortega: do you support bring-your-own-kms (BYOK) and HSM?
[03:36] Priya Kapoor: yes we have KMS integrations and HSM support for private deployments; hosted can integrate with our managed encryption, but for strict compliance we usually recommend dedicated or private where you retain key control
[03:48] Maya Chen: good. so for a quickstart, how many free credits do you typically give and whats time to first token?
[03:55] Jordan Ellis: our PLG quickstart usually includes starter credits sufficient for several thousand requests and we aim to get customers to their first successful request within a few hours — TTFT is often under an hour if you follow the quickstart and share a sample prompt set
[04:12] Raul Ortega: so hypothetically - if we take quickstart hosted route to validate, and then move to dedicated gpu pools, is there a migration path? or is it a forklift?
[04:22] Priya Kapoor: there's a migration path — same api and routing layer. you can pin model versions and routing policies; for most customers it's an easy switch, we do model variant fallback so you can test hosted and then cut over to dedicated without significant client changes
[04:40] Jordan Ellis: can i ask about integrations? do you need sso or just api keys for initial testing?
[04:47] Maya Chen: initial test keys are fine, but eventual we need SAML SSO for dev and RBAC for team roles and audit history
[04:55] Priya Kapoor: we support SAML SSO, SCIM user provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC in the console. also per-route usage and token-level cost breakdowns if you want to track spend per feature
[05:12] Sofia Alvarez: what about prompt engineering and safety — do you provide eval tooling or regression alerts?
[05:18] Priya Kapoor: yes thats part of Redwood Optimize offering; you can tie prompt sets to evals and get regression alerts when a new model or quantization profile hurts quality. during pilots we usually run smoke checks on a prompt-set you share
[05:33] Raul Ortega: onboarding question — network side, if we pick private VPC option how does traffic route? do we need expressconnect?
[05:40] Priya Kapoor: for VPC deployments you either peer our control plane or deploy our on-prem bundle; traffic can stay on your network, we support direct connect and VPN options. sequencing depends on your infra team comfort and security review timelines
[06:00] Jordan Ellis: let's talk about cost models briefly — hosted is usage-based, dedicated is reserved capacity commitments monthly/annual. do you have budget ranges yet?
[06:11] Maya Chen: we have internal budget for pilot, not final for production — want a rough sense of committed spend if we go dedicated (estimate per GPU pool or per qps)
[06:21] Jordan Ellis: understood, i'll send a pilot pricing sheet. for 50 QPS at modest token sizes, we usually model a dedicated pool with X GPUs, i'll include ballpark ranges and example unit economics so you can see cost per 1k tokens and per-request
[06:36] Sofia Alvarez: one more question — are there any managed fallbacks? like if a model is slower or capacity constrained do you have an automatic fallback to a cheaper model?
[06:44] Priya Kapoor: yes that's a common pattern — smart routing can fall back by policy to cheaper variants or different regions; we can set automatic fallback to keep you online if capacity is constrained
[06:58] Raul Ortega: from a dev point of view, whats the SDK story? we have a node backend and some rust services
[07:05] Jordan Ellis: we have official SDKs for python, node, and community libs for go/rust, plus a rest api. most customers integrate via the SDK and use our streaming responses for interactive experiences
[07:18] Maya Chen: ok good. how about compliance artifacts — SOC2, ISO, pen test reports?
[07:25] Jordan Ellis: we have a security pack and can share SOC2 attestation, iso certs where applicable, and past pentest summary for enterprise review — i'll attach to the follow up email
[07:35] Priya Kapoor: also note that for private deploys we can provide network diagrams and architecture runbooks for your security team
[07:44] Jordan Ellis: so, to be concrete about a pilot — sounds like you want: hosted quickstart to validate prompt latency and quality within two weeks, followed by a dedicated pilot for throughput testing. correct?
[07:57] Maya Chen: yes that sounds right. initial validation in hosted to get TTFT and QA, then a dedicated pilot if the numbers look good
[08:06] Raul Ortega: i'd like a perf run using our prompt set and a synthetic QPS profile, can you do that and show p50/p95/p99?
[08:13] Priya Kapoor: absolutely, if you share the prompt set and an example traffic shape i'll run a benchmark on both hosted and a dedicated config and share results. for hosted it will be representative but dedicated will show our optimized kernel and batching benefits
[08:28] Jordan Ellis: ill also include a sample agreement and the quickstart credit process — the quickstart gives you a sandbox key, sample quotas, and we can help instrument traces in the console
[08:38] Sofia Alvarez: whats the typical ramp from quickstart to pilot in your experience?
[08:44] Jordan Ellis: if security signoff is easy and you share prompts in 1 week, you can be into a 2-3 week quickstart and then spin up dedicated pilot in 4-8 weeks depending on procurement
[08:56] Raul Ortega: procurement note — we have a security questionnaire template and an NDA already, will send those over, how fast can you return the answers?
[09:04] Priya Kapoor: we usually respond to standard security questionnaires in 3-5 business days, and we have a standard NDA and MSA for pilots to accelerate procurement
[09:12] Maya Chen: ok good. a couple of edge questions — do you support model quantization options? we plan to try int8 quantized variants for cost-saving
[09:20] Priya Kapoor: yes we support quantization profiles and can recommend for your workload, Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization vs model variant tradeoffs and we can run quality regressions as part of the pilot
[09:33] Jordan Ellis: competitor question — anything you like about openai or anthro that we should match for this pilot?
[09:40] Maya Chen: openai has predictable latency and a familiar SDK, anthro gave us a nice safety layer on their stack, we want the best of both: simplicity, predictable latency, and strong security controls
[09:53] Priya Kapoor: understood — we'll focus on quick TTFT, a small perf matrix, and the security pack in the follow up
[10:00] Jordan Ellis: ok next steps recap: i'll send pricing, security docs, and quickstart onboarding steps. priya will run scheduling for the performance demo and benchmark once you share prompts. maya to share the sample prompt set and expected qps.
[10:16] Maya Chen: sounds good, i'll put the prompt set in a shared drive today and invite priya/ jordan.
[10:24] Raul Ortega: i'll also attach our security questionnaire and procurement timelines.
[10:30] Sofia Alvarez: one ask — can you include a simple cost model that shows cost if we stay hosted vs move to dedicate at 10k requests/day?
[10:38] Jordan Ellis: yes i'll include example unit economics for a few traffic sizes including 10k req/day and 50 qps sustained profiles
[10:46] Maya Chen: perfect. any blockers for us to start the quickstart today?
[10:50] Priya Kapoor: no blockers on our side, quickstart only needs an email and we'll provision sandbox keys, but for your evaluation we'd prefer the prompt set to ground the perf run
[10:58] Jordan Ellis: great, we can close there. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the perf session
[11:05] Maya Chen: thanks all, appreciate it
[11:08] Raul Ortega: thanks, bye
[11:10] Jordan Ellis: bye

End of transcript.
